column1: # Shelf — entity-resolution labels for the monitors category (M7).
# One line per (offer, seed product) pair: is this listing a purchasable variant of that product?
# Written by hand from listing titles alone — before the resolver had scored a single monitor
# listing — over the storefront JSON captured 2026-09-16 (six retailers, 349 listings, 127 seed
# products). One representative variant URL stands for each distinct product title at a retailer.
# Policy, carried from the keyboards set. A listing matches when it is the seed product in any
# purchasable new form: a colourway, a panel finish (matte / glossy / Gorilla Glass), a "with hub"
# or "without hub" configuration, a listing that spells the model with or without its suffix
# ("45GS95QE" for "45GS95QE-B"). It does not match when it is a sibling model in the same line
# (PX279 Prime Neo vs PX279 Wave, GM27-FQS vs GM27-CFX, U3223QE vs U3225QE, Spectrum Black 27
# vs 32), used / open-box / refurbished / B-stock stock of the product (a real price, but not the
# product's), a bundle with other goods (a keyboard, a mouse, a hub, a cable — whether or not the
# word "bundle" appears), a two-monitor combo, or an accessory (a stand, an arm). A title that
# states no size for a product sold in two sizes ("Spectrum Black") is labeled a non-match for
# both: the label is what the title says, not what the labeler happens to know.
# Columns (tab-separated): offer_url  title  brand  model  match  note. `title` is for the reader;
# `shelf eval resolution` keys the offer by URL and the product by brand + model.
